Finance Notes for MBA, BBA and BBM Students

Free topic-wise notes on financial markets, accounting, corporate finance, derivatives, banking and economics. Each one has definitions, formulas, worked examples and exam-style questions, and links to related topics, so you can follow one idea to the next.

New to markets? Start with what the stock market is. Need a word explained? Use the glossary of 387 terms. For structured learning in English and Hindi, take the free courses, then test yourself with the final test.

Markets and investing

Indian Financial System: Markets, Institutions and Regulators

A financial system moves money from people who have savings to people and businesses who need funds. This guide maps its four parts: institutions, markets, instruments and regulators.

2 min read

What Is the Stock Market? Meaning, How It Works and Key Terms

The stock market is where shares of listed companies are bought and sold through regulated exchanges. Companies use it to raise money, and investors use it to own part of a business and to trade that ownership.

2 min read

Primary vs Secondary Market: IPO, FPO, Rights Issue and QIP

New securities are sold in the primary market, and existing ones are traded in the secondary market. This guide compares the two and sets out each way a company can raise money.

2 min read

Types of Shares: Equity vs Preference Shares, and Share Capital

Companies raise ownership capital mainly through equity shares and preference shares. This guide compares them, explains the kinds of share capital, and clears up the three values of a share.

2 min read

Risk and Return: Portfolio Theory, Beta, CAPM and Sharpe Ratio

Higher expected return comes with higher risk, but not all risk is rewarded. This guide covers how risk is measured, how diversification reduces it, and how CAPM prices it, with fully worked numbers.

2 min read

Mutual Funds Explained: Types, NAV, Structure, SIP and Costs

A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a professionally managed portfolio. This guide covers its structure, how NAV is worked out, the fund types, and what it costs.

2 min read

Accounting and financial statements

What Is a Balance Sheet? Format, Example and How to Read It

A balance sheet shows what a company owns, what it owes and what belongs to its shareholders on one specific date. This guide covers the equation behind it, its format under Indian law, and how to read it.

2 min read

Profit and Loss Statement: Format, Example and Key Profit Lines

The profit and loss statement shows how much a company earned and spent over a period, and what was left. This guide walks through it line by line, using a worked example.

2 min read

Cash Flow Statement: Indirect Method, Format and Worked Example

A company can show a profit and still run out of cash. The cash flow statement shows where cash actually came from and went, split across three activities. Under Ind AS 7 and AS 3, most companies prepare it by the indirect method.

2 min read

Ratio Analysis: Formulas, Examples and How to Interpret Them

Ratios turn the numbers in financial statements into comparisons that mean something. This guide gives the main formulas by category, all worked on the same company, and shows how to read them.

2 min read

Corporate finance

Time Value of Money: Present Value, Future Value and Annuities

A rupee today is worth more than a rupee next year, because it can earn a return in the meantime and inflation erodes it. Almost all of finance rests on this idea, and this guide gives the formulas with worked numbers.

2 min read

Capital Budgeting: NPV, IRR, Payback and Profitability Index

Capital budgeting is how a company decides which long-term projects to invest in. This guide applies every major method to one project, and shows why NPV is usually preferred.

2 min read

Cost of Capital: WACC Formula, Cost of Debt and Cost of Equity

The cost of capital is the minimum return a company must earn to keep its lenders and shareholders satisfied. It is the discount rate in capital budgeting and valuation, and this guide works it out step by step.

2 min read

Leverage and Capital Structure: DOL, DFL, DCL and Theories

Leverage means using fixed costs to magnify results. Fixed operating costs magnify the effect of sales on profit, and fixed interest magnifies the effect of profit on earnings per share. This guide measures both.

2 min read

Working Capital Management: Cycle, Inventory and Receivables

Working capital is the money tied up in running the business each day. Too little and bills go unpaid; too much and capital sits idle. This guide covers how it is measured and managed.

2 min read

Mergers and Acquisitions: Types, Process, Swap Ratio and Synergy

Companies combine to grow faster, cut costs or enter new markets. This guide covers the forms of combination, how a deal is done, and how it is valued, with a swap ratio example.

2 min read

Derivatives

What Are Derivatives? Forwards, Futures, Options and Swaps

A derivative is a contract whose value depends on something else, such as a share, an index, a commodity or a currency. This guide compares the four main types and explains why they exist.

2 min read

What Is a Futures Contract? Margin, Pricing and Examples

A futures contract is a standardised agreement to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a future date, traded on an exchange. This guide works through a trade, margin, daily settlement and how futures are priced.

2 min read

What Are Options? Call and Put, Premium, Pay-offs and Pricing

An option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price by a set date. This guide covers calls and puts with worked pay-offs, how the premium is made up, and what moves it.

2 min read

Banking and fixed income

Types of Bank Accounts in India: Savings, Current, FD, RD and NRI

Banks offer accounts for everyday money, for businesses, for savings over time, and for non-residents. This guide compares them, and explains how money moves between them.

2 min read

Fixed Deposit (FD): Types, Interest, Tax, Auto-Sweep and FD vs RD

A fixed deposit is a sum placed with a bank or NBFC for a set period at an agreed interest rate. This guide covers every type of FD, how the interest is worked out, how it is taxed, and how it compares with other choices.

3 min read

Recurring Deposit (RD): Meaning, Interest Formula and RD vs SIP

A recurring deposit lets you save a fixed amount every month and earn a fixed rate of interest. It suits people without a lump sum, and this guide covers the working, the tax, and how it compares with an FD and a SIP.

2 min read

Bonds and Debentures: Types, Pricing, Yield and Credit Ratings

A bond is a loan you give to a government or a company, in return for interest and repayment on a set date. This guide covers the types, how to price a bond, and why prices fall when interest rates rise.

2 min read

Economics and policy

RBI Monetary Policy: Repo Rate, CRR, SLR and Inflation Targeting

Monetary policy is how the RBI manages interest rates and the money supply to control inflation and support growth. This guide explains each tool and how a rate change reaches you. The rates themselves change, so check the RBI for current values.

2 min read

GDP, Inflation and Fiscal Policy: Macroeconomics for Students

Macroeconomics looks at the economy as a whole: output, prices, jobs and government finances. This guide covers the key measures and how the government influences them, and why investors follow them.

2 min read
